limits: One screening trial per configuration; startup and worker warm-up excluded.
No training or optimizer updates were performed, and production defaults were not changed.
All 100 game summaries and 33,543 numerical observations/actions matched; recurrent memories, behavior probabilities and values were not bit-identical.
Different inference batches produced floating-point differences up to 4.95e-6. These could affect subsequent training numerically.

The two collectors ran simultaneously after an explicit warm-up barrier, with 45.5 ms start skew. Their timing is the union of both timed intervals; CPU totals include both parents and all game workers.
No other training or benchmarks were run concurrently; desktop background work and thermal conditions were not controlled.
A spot check during the 64-worker experiment observed host swap use rise from 1.7 GiB before the sweep to 5.7 GiB; memory and swapping were not continuously profiled.
